_note: The vital-sign contract for GilbertOne's /assistant/v1/vitals route. It is a server-side contract in the shape of the knowledge federation's own files: read by apps/assistant-api/src/lib/vitals.ts and by nothing that ships to a phone, so it has no generator and no line in the generated-files registry. Every number here is a plausibility bound — the outside of which a typed or transmitted value is refused as a mistake — and never a clinical threshold, a triage cut-off or a scoring input: deciding what a reading MEANS for a patient is Clinical's, under a protocol a governance board has ratified, and none has. The LOINC codes name the observation and the UCUM units name the measure, so a value is never read as another; the codes pass the LOINC check digit that scripts/knowledge-codes.mjs validates. Nothing in this file diagnoses, scores or triages.

consent.why: A reading is the person's own health information the moment it is captured, so the agreement comes first and a reading that arrives without it is refused rather than stored.

darkForRealDevices.why: A real device, a HealthKit source and a Health Connect source each put a certified reading into the clinical record, which is a processing of special personal information that POPIA s57 holds behind a Data Protection Impact Assessment nobody has completed. Until it is, the route answers only synthetic readings, and only where the deployment switched testing on.

testing.why: The one door that opens the route while the DPIA is not done: a deployment that sets this variable to this exact value accepts a synthetic manual reading for its own tests. Absent it, or set to anything else, every reading is refused and the route is dark.

staleness.why: A reading older than a day is stale: it describes a person who may have changed since, so it is refused rather than handed to a clinician as current. The bound is a freshness rule, not a clinical one.

deviceAllowlist.why: The certified devices whose readings this deployment accepts. It is empty: no device has been registered against a completed DPIA, so a deviceRef that is not on this list is refused, and with the list empty every real-device reading is. A device joins only by a deliberate edit here, after the assessment that darkForRealDevices names.
